newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Dadas fall sends Slovenia shares to all-time low.
newsitem.headline: Dadas fall sends Slovenia shares to all-time low.

text.p: Slovenian shares tumbled five percent to reach an all-time low on Monday, knocked down as investors bailed out of market heavyweight Dadas.
Financial consultancy Dadas shed more than 50 percent on market rumours its brokerage may be banned from trading.
"There may be some insider information involved in today's fall (of Dadas), because from the information we have it cannot be explained," said Nina Jarc, a trader at Nova Ljubljanska banka.
In March, the Securities Market Agency started procedures to ban the broking arm of Dadas from trading, accusing it of rigging prices by trading among its affiliated companies.
The market watchdog said it would not comment on the case until it was over.
Since March, Dadas shares have tumbled 95 percent, pulling the index down as much as 42 percent.
"It's obvious that pessimism on the market is rampant due to a lack of information about Dadas. But prices of other shares are expected to stabilise," said Danilo Grasic, a trader at Creditanstalt.
He said that while Dadas may continue falling, further losses of other shares were unlikely because most investors believed prices have already bottomed out.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 47.17 points to 893.88. The previous all-time-low was reached on July 19 at 910.74.
* 17 shares fell and two rose, while four were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 72.5 million tolars from 68.6 million.
* Financial consultancy Dadas was the most actively traded and the leading decliner, falling 53.05 percent to 12,811 tolars on volume of 2,177 shares for total turnover of 27.9 million tolars.

* Drug company Lek, which released its half year business results today, was the biggest gainer, firming 5.47 percent to 13,395 tolars on volume of 95 shares for total turnover of 1.3 million tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
